title: Israel-Hamas truce begins and first hostages are freed
body:
On 24 November 2023, a four-day truce between Israel and Hamas took effect in the Gaza Strip, mediated by Qatar with the United States and Egypt. Hours later, Hamas released 24 captives who had been held in Gaza for almost seven weeks. They included 13 Israelis, 10 Thai nationals and one Filipino citizen. The International Committee of the Red Cross transported them from Gaza to the Rafah border crossing with Egypt.

Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said the Thai and Filipino captives were freed outside the framework of the Israel-Hamas agreement. In exchange, Israel released 39 Palestinian prisoners, described as women and children, of whom 33 were freed in the West Bank and handed to the Red Cross and six were released from a Jerusalem prison.

The deal provided for Hamas to free 50 women and children out of 237 captives, as cited by Al Jazeera, and for Israel to release 150 Palestinian women and children from its prisons. The pause could be extended by one day for every 10 additional hostages released. Before 7 October, about 5,200 Palestinians were held in Israeli prisons, according to Al Jazeera. Israel stressed that the truce did not mean the end of the war, and Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant was reported to have said the respite would be short.
